m: The {Wizard} races down the {Staircase} of the {Mansion} in a sack race against his own broom. At the bottom a *finish line* of glowing tape snaps across his beard and confetti pours from the chandeliers. The race is **finished**, the broom sulks, and the wizard declares the whole house **finished** too, so the walls politely fold themselves up like a deckchair.

The {Sheriff} pops up through the {Trapdoor} of a tiny {Hut} with a *war club* and a *small speech bubble* that shouts orders all by itself. Bonk, bonk: the club hammers in tent pegs, a table, a flagpole, a whole wedding marquee. In five minutes the bubble squeaks, Everything is **set up**! and the sheriff **sets up** a deckchair to admire it.

The {Sheriff} drops through the {Trapdoor} into the {Beehive} holding a giant *stencil* and a can of yellow spray paint. Every bee that buzzes past gets sprayed into exactly the same **form**: same stripes, same wings, same tiny moustache. The queen fills in a **form** to complain, but the form, of course, comes out the same shape too.

The {Sailor} yanks open the {Trapdoor} of his {Hut} and a *rainbow* shoots out like a fire hose. It splashes **colour** over everything: the cat turns violet, the kettle goes tangerine, the sailor's beard turns electric green. He tries to mop it all up, but the mop just comes out in every **colour** at once.

The {Lifeguard} lifts a {Trapdoor} at the bottom of the {Pool} and a *pathway* of paving stones unrolls out of it like a carpet. It drains the water and keeps going, out the gate, across town, until it becomes a four-lane **road**. Cars honk past the diving board, and the lifeguard blows her whistle at a lorry for running on the **road**.

The {Juggler} hauls a struggling *small speech bubble* up through a {Trapdoor} in the {Beach}. Before it can float off and forget what it said, he ties it down with a *coiled rope* and pins it into his notebook. Now every word it squeaks is **recorded**, and he plays the **recording** back to the seagulls each morning.

The {Ninja} slides down the banister of the {Mansion}'s {Staircase} clutching a compass whose needle has fainted and points only *south*. He follows it through a wall, a greenhouse and a flock of geese, all flying **south** for the winter. He lands in a hammock on a sunny beach, very far **south**, still in his black pyjamas.

The {Pirate} kicks open the door to the {Inn}'s {Basement} and finds it stacked to the ceiling with *goods*: boxes of rubber ducks, socks and tinned pineapple. He slaps a price tag on each crate and bellows, Finest **product** in the seven seas! By sunset the innkeeper is buying back his own **products** at triple the price.

The {Jockey} opens a {Trapdoor} under the {Pool} and finds a *standing person* in slippers, reading by a *candle* in a dry little flat beneath the water. The person **lives** there, with a sofa, a fridge and a goldfish swimming in the ceiling. The jockey moves in too, because anywhere with a candle and a fridge is a fine place to **live**.

The {Gardener} drags an *announcer* out of the {Trapdoor} at the top of the {Tower} and hands him a megaphone. The announcer **tells** the whole city everything: who stole the gnome, who drowned the tulips, who snores. Neighbours run outside in their dressing gowns as he **tells** them secrets even the gardener didn't know.

The {Lifeguard} opens a {Trapdoor} on a raft in the middle of the {Lake}, and a *big man* climbs out with a sack of *rice*. He tips it into a hundred bowls and sorts every grain by **kind**: long, short, sticky, brown, purple. Ducks queue up to choose their favourite **kind**, and one swan demands a kind that doesn't exist.

The {Cheerleader} stomps up and down the {Staircase} of the {Youth Hostel} waving pom-poms and chanting, Who has seen my *fur coat*? She **seeks** it in every dorm, under bunks, inside backpacks, even in the toaster. At last she finds the fur coat walking about on the landing by itself, also **seeking** its owner.

The {Juggler} climbs out of a {Trapdoor} in the {Museum} and a *helping hand* passes him a tiny model *house* with a map glued to its roof. **According to** the map, the treasure is under the dinosaur. He digs there and finds only a sock, but the hand taps the map again: **according to** this, the sock is the treasure.

The {Chef} wants to bake one loaf in the {Jungle}, but first a monkey makes her climb a vine {Staircase} with a *grain stalk* and a twelve-page *petition*. Step by step: stamp the petition, thresh the stalk, ask a parrot, sign again. The **process** takes three weeks, and by the end of the **process** the bread is a fossil.

The {Baker} sneaks into a {Basement} under the frozen {Lake} where the *north* wind lives in a jam jar. He unscrews the lid and a polar gale blasts him and his doughnuts straight **north**, past puffins, past icebergs, past a confused polar bear. He lands on the North Pole with his icing frozen solid, pointing **north** forever.

The {Baker} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Yen Exchange} as a *road* winds right up the wall to meet him. A *strong arm* reaches out of the gutter and shoves every car to the **side** of the road, one by one, until they dangle off the edge. The baker sells them buns from the **side**, leaning over the drop.

The {Sailor} digs in the {Basement} of the {Beehive} and finds a tiny *grave* with a bee-sized headstone. Here lies the drone who **died** of boredom, it reads. Suddenly the drone pops up, yawning, complains that being **dead** was even duller than being alive, and buzzes off to find something to do.

The {Jockey} gallops across the {Rooftop} of the {Hangar} with a giant *stretched bow*, firing **sheets** of paper instead of arrows. Thwip! One **sheet** wraps a pilot, another a plane, a third the whole windsock. By evening the hangar is papered over like a birthday parcel, and the jockey counts every sheet: three thousand and one.

The {Gardener} is up on the {Rooftop} of the {Island} lighthouse when a *wild boar* trots up carrying a *small speech bubble* in its tusks. The bubble nags: You **should** water the plants. You **should** wear a hat. You should not be on a roof. The gardener flings it into the sea, where it keeps advising the fish.

The {Juggler} sits with *crossed legs* on the {Rooftop} of the {Cat Café}, and a long line of cats climbs up to **hand over** their toys: mice, balls, string, one stolen sausage. He juggles them all, then **hands over** each one to the next cat in the queue, so nobody ever gets their own toy back.

The {Gardener} climbs onto the {Rooftop} of the {Waiting Room} with a giant *compass* and scratches perfect circles on the tiles. Inside each circle he paints a **rule**: No humming. No sighing. No looking at the clock. Patients below hear the compass scraping and obey every **rule**, sitting perfectly round and perfectly still.

The {Wizard} pulls a lever and the {Trapdoor} of the {Mansion} drops open, releasing a *swarm* of glowing moths. He tries to count them: one, two, three, all the way to **ten thousand**! They cover the curtains, the piano, the butler's bald head. The butler sighs and starts dusting **ten thousand** tiny wings, one by one.

The {Cheerleader} cartwheels into the {Museum}'s {Basement} and a *grabbing hand* shoots out of a crate. It **takes** her pom-poms, the guard's hat, a mummy's bandages and a dinosaur's toe. She chants, Give it back! but the hand just **takes** that too and stuffs the whole chant into its pocket.

The {Lifeguard} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Spa} as a *pulling hand* grabs the plug chain of the hot tub. It **pulls** and **pulls**: out come the water, a rubber duck, three snoozing guests in towels, and finally a very surprised octopus. The lifeguard grabs its wrist and **pulls** it back before it drains the sky.

The {Gardener} plants a *tree* by the {Staircase} of his {Hut}, and a *visitor* arrives carrying a ruler. The visitor saws the tree into straight planks and nails them into a giant **grid** of squares over the steps. Now every guest must hop from square to square, and the gardener plays noughts and crosses on the **grid** all summer.

The {Wizard} peers up from a {Trapdoor} in the {Hangar} at a *king* who takes a huge breath, his *diaphragm* swelling like a balloon. He blows at a paper plane, **hoping** it will fly. It flops. He breathes in again, bigger, full of **hope**, and this time the plane, the hangar doors and the wizard's hat all sail off together.

The {Juggler} skates down an icy {Staircase} at the {Ice Rink} juggling an *alarm clock* that goes off in mid-air. RRRING! It wakes up his whole body: he **feels** the cold in his toes, the bump on his bottom, the wobble in his knees. He **feels** everything at once and sits on the ice, laughing.

The {Sheriff} rises out of a {Trapdoor} in the {Pool} wearing a cape and performs a *magic trick*: he pulls a whole dolphin out of his hat. The crowd gasps. Asked for his secret, he says it is pure **technique**: wrist flick, wink, and a very patient dolphin. Children copy the **technique** all afternoon and pull out only wet socks.

Down in the {Basement} under the {Boxing Ring}, the {Lifeguard} follows a *herald* blowing a trumpet and a *page* carrying the gloves. The herald **leads** the march round and round the ring, and fighters fall in behind like ducklings. Soon a hundred boxers are being **led** in circles, and nobody remembers who was meant to fight.

The {Gardener} opens a {Trapdoor} on a floating dock in the {Lagoon}, and out come a hundred *joined hands* holding one enormous sandwich. Everyone takes a bite: fish, turtles, the gardener, a passing pelican. The sandwich is **common** property, so the lagoon shares one **common** lunch, and nobody can let go to wipe their mouth.

The {Cheerleader} pops through a {Trapdoor} in the {Ice Rink} and tests the ice by dropping a *stone* on it, then whacking it with an *ox horn*. Not a crack. She stamps, jumps, invites a herd of oxen to tap dance. Now she is **certain**, absolutely **certain** the ice will hold. Then the ice machine rumbles in and she is slightly less sure.

On the {Staircase} down to the {Swan Pond}, the {Chef} hands a *spindle* of thread to a *standing person* on the step below. They **pass it on** to the next person, and the next, all the way down to a swan, who knits it into a scarf. The scarf is then **passed on** back up the stairs, unravelling as it goes.

The {Sheriff} climbs onto the {Rooftop} of the {Beehive} and finds a *teacher* with a tiny chalkboard giving lessons to the bees. Buzz is spelled with two Zs! the **teacher** cries, rapping the board. The bees take notes, the sheriff takes notes, and by sunset the **teacher** has taught the honey to sit up straight.

On the {Rooftop} of the pavilion at the {Swan Pond}, the {Gardener} shades her eyes with her *right hand* and sits beside a *watcher* with binoculars. Together they **watch** two swans fight over a bread roll. The swans notice, stop, turn round, and **watch** them right back, and nobody blinks for an hour.

On the {Rooftop} above the {Boxing Ring}, the {Cheerleader} finds the skylight furred over with green *moss*. She shakes her pom-poms and a shower of *water drops* rinses it until the glass is perfectly **clear**. Now the boxers below can see the sky, the stars and her high kicks, all crystal **clear**.

The {Juggler} balances on the {Rooftop} of the {Inn} juggling a giant *clock* that shouts **Now!** every second. Now! Now! Now! Guests lean out of the windows in their nightcaps, but the clock never says yesterday or tomorrow, only **now**. Finally the innkeeper yells, Bed, **now**! and everyone obeys.

The {Cheerleader} high-kicks across the {Rooftop} of the {Yeti Cave} with scissors taped to her shoes. Every kick makes a *cut*: icicles, the yeti's fringe, a snowman's scarf, the washing line. The yeti tries to stop her, but she **cuts** him off mid-roar, then **cuts** a perfect snowflake out of his fur.

The {Yogi} opens a {Trapdoor} in the {Mint}'s floor and finds a sunny **courtyard** dug into a *hillside*. Coins roll down the slope in a race and tumble across a *finish line* painted on the cobbles. The yogi sits cross-legged in the middle of the **courtyard** while pennies whizz round him like tiny racing cars.

The {Robot} stands guard at the {Trapdoor} of the {Hangar} until a *small speech bubble* floats up and says, Please **let** me go *upstairs*. The robot beeps, thinks, and steps aside. It **lets** the bubble through, then a parrot, then a whole marching band, until upstairs is so crowded the roof politely lifts its hat.

The {Sheriff} climbs the waxy {Staircase} of the {Beehive} and meets a *lone bird* holding a *small speech bubble* full of answers. Ask me anything, it chirps. The sheriff asks the capital of Peru, the queen's birthday, his own shoe size, and the bird **knows** every one. Now the bees won't do anything until the bird says it **knows** best.

The {Hunter} crouches under the {Trapdoor} of the {Boathouse}, waiting for the right **time** to pounce on a giant pike. He checks his watch, the tide, the moon, his watch again. When the **time** finally comes, he leaps up, the trapdoor slams on his hat, and the pike paddles off in his canoe, laughing, right on **time**.

The {Dentist} pops through a {Trapdoor} on a tiny {Island} wearing a *belt* with a hundred pockets. He **brings** everything: toothbrushes, a coconut-sized drill, floss for a whale. Castaways rush over, and he pulls a sofa and a piano out of the belt too. Next time, they beg, **bring** a boat.

In the {Basement} of the {Tower}, the {Dentist} follows a *cobra* that sways ahead of him while a giant *thumb* points the way. Up the spiral stairs they go, the snake **leading** and hissing directions, the thumb jabbing left and right. They **lead** him to a room full of crocodiles with toothache, his biggest clients yet.

The {Jockey} stands on a treehouse {Rooftop} in the {Jungle}, refereeing a *tug of war* between a gorilla and an elephant. Both **strive** with all their might, grunting, sweating, digging in their heels, while the rope stretches across three valleys. Each one **strives** so hard that the treehouse is yanked off and lands in a river.

The {Yogi} opens a {Trapdoor} in the {Dunes} and a *road* unrolls across the sand. A fluffy *cloud* floats down and parks on it like a lorry. He loads it with camels, watermelons and a grand piano, and the cloud **transports** them all across the desert, raining on anyone who complains about the **transport**.

The {Shepherd} pops out of a {Trapdoor} in the {Cat Café} just as a *dancer* starts tickling every cat with a stick of *bamboo*. The cats **laugh**, then the customers, then the coffee machine snorts froth. Soon the shepherd is **laughing** so hard he rolls under a table, and the dancer tickles him too.

The {Firefighter} is stranded on the {Rooftop} of a cabin by the {Lake} when a giant *swan* lands beside her and offers its back. She hops on and they **fly** over the water, ladder and all. Ducks stare as she points the hose backwards like a jet pack and **flies** even faster, spraying rainbows.

On the {Rooftop} of a hut in the {Jungle}, the {Firefighter} uncorks a bottle labelled *wind*. Whoosh! A howling **wind** blows the monkeys out of the trees, spins the parrots like pinwheels and puffs her helmet up like a balloon. She tries to hose it back into the bottle, but you cannot hose the **wind**.

The {Baker} descends through a {Trapdoor} at the bottom of the {Pool} onto a *step* made of baguettes. Each **step** he takes bakes another crusty step below. Crunch, crunch: ten thousand **steps** later he reaches the centre of the earth, which is, disappointingly, a bakery with a very long queue.

In the {Basement} of the {Island} lighthouse, the {Gardener} whacks a *coiled rope* with a *cane*, and with every whack it **changes**: into a snake, a hosepipe, a necklace, a strand of spaghetti. He keeps tapping, delighted, until it **changes** into a second gardener, who grabs the cane and tries it on him.

The {Sheriff} sits on the {Rooftop} of the {Boathouse} with a *cane* tied to a long *twisted vine*, fishing for parcels in the river. Every cast **receives** something: a letter, a cake, a grumpy goose in a box. He signs for each one with a flourish, and soon the postman just throws everything at him, so he **receives** the whole town's mail.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Funfair}'s haunted house, the {Gardener} spots a *tree* growing out of the chimney. She gives it a furious *glare*, and the tree is so scared it pulls up its **roots** and runs. The **roots** scuttle down the dodgems like spider legs, and the tree hides behind the candyfloss stall, shaking.

The {Gardener} bursts up through the {Trapdoor} of the {Mansion} with a *drying rack* on his back, ready to **do** every job at once. He hangs laundry, peels potatoes, polishes spoons and dries the cat, all on the rack's arms. The butler asks what else he can **do**, and the rack starts ironing the butler.

The {Zookeeper} climbs through the {Trapdoor} of a half-finished {Tower} as an *announcer* bellows through a megaphone, Lay the *road*! Elephants stamp bricks into a road that spirals up the walls, and giraffes stack the top floors. They **build** all night, and by morning the zoo has **built** a skyscraper where the penguins live in the penthouse.

The {Yogi} meditates on the {Staircase} of the {Mansion} until a huge *speech bubble* floats out of his ear. It overflows with **words**, and they spill down the steps like marbles: banana, tremendous, hiccup, moustache. The maids sweep up **words** all afternoon, and the butler pockets the long ones to show off at dinner.

The {Lifeguard} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Yen Exchange} with a giant *ear* that hears traders yelling on both sides of a *mountain pass* made of paperwork. She blasts her whistle, and the traders shuffle across the pass to shake hands. The two sides **unite**, then hug, then **unite** so tightly they become one enormous, very confused banker.

Halfway up the {Staircase} of the {Beehive}, the {Chef} stops because a *helping hand* is **holding** up a tiny golden *temple* full of buzzing monks. Don't drop it! the bees beg. So the chef takes over and **holds** it, then sneezes, and the hand catches both chef and temple, balancing them on one finger.

In the {Basement} below the {Pool}, the {Zookeeper} climbs a *stepladder* and strings *silk thread* from wall to wall. He **organizes** the chaos: flippers on one thread, rubber rings on another, sleepy seals clipped on by their tails. By lunchtime the whole basement is **organized** like a washing line, and the seals are sorted by snore.

In a {Basement} under the {Lake}, the {Magician} watches a *busy mother* with eight arms make sandwiches. She makes one for **every** duck, **every** frog, every fish, every pebble. The magician waves his wand to help, and suddenly there are two of her, then four, until **every** creature in the lake has its own lunchbox.

The {Juggler} bursts from a {Trapdoor} in the {Beach} with a bucket of *water drops* for a *trimmed hedge* that is wilting in the sun. He juggles the drops onto its leaves, one by one, and it perks up. Soon every plant on the beach queues for **aid**, so he opens a first-**aid** tent with a sign: Hedges First.

The {Chef} pushes a wooden *cart* across the {Rooftop} of her {Hut}, steering with a saucepan. She bolts on an engine, a horn and four doughnuts for wheels, and the cart coughs into a roaring **car**. It leaps off the edge, and the chef zooms off to the shops in the world's tastiest **car**.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Inn}, the {Cheerleader} finds her *parents* sunbathing in matching swimsuits. They leap up with pom-poms and cheer her name louder than any stadium. Every guest leans out to see the most embarrassing **parents** in the world, and she hides behind the chimney while each **parent** waves a banner with her baby photo.

The {Juggler} sprints up a sandy {Staircase} on the {Beach}, followed by a *chaser* who is **extremely** fast. He climbs a palm *tree* to escape, but the chaser climbs it too, **extremely** quickly, and they reach the very tip at the same moment. The tree bends like a catapult and flings them both into the sea, extremely wet.

The {Lifeguard} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Inn}, and every step sprouts a tree until a whole *grove* fills the hallway. By the top floor the inn is thick **woods**: owls in the wardrobes, deer at the breakfast bar, a fox at reception. Guests check in with compasses and get lost in the **woods** on the way to the bathroom.

The {Firefighter} walks down the {Staircase} into the {Pool} at night, where a giant *pressing hand* is ironing **clothes** on the flat face of the *moon*. Shirts, socks and swimsuits come out crisp and silver. She hands up her soggy uniform, and the moon hands back the shiniest **clothes** in town.

The {King} drops through the {Trapdoor} into the {Wine Cellar} wearing an *archer's ring*, and his *standing heart* starts pounding like a drum. He shoots arrows at runaway corks, **quick**, quicker, quickest, until the cellar is a blur. When the queen walks in, he hides every bottle at lightning speed, very **quick** indeed.

The {Baker} lifts the {Trapdoor} of the {Mansion} to reveal a secret *workshop* full of hammers, ovens and spinning gadgets. Every problem in the house drops down to him: a leaking tap, a squeaky door, a duke stuck in a vase. He **handles** them all with a rolling pin and hangs up a sign: No job too odd to **handle**.

The {Yogi} opens a {Trapdoor} on the {Beach} and finds a *judge* in a wig arguing with a *small speech bubble* about sandcastles. They **discuss** towers, moats, flags and the correct number of seashells. The tide comes in, the sandcastle melts, and they keep **discussing** it, up to their necks in the sea.

In the {Basement} of the {Hangar}, the {Wizard} holds up a *candle* and sees glowing *footsteps* marching across the floor. They all head **towards** the far wall, then up it, then **towards** the roof, where a hatch opens onto a waiting jumbo jet. The wizard follows them in his slippers, clutching his candle.

The {Yogi} sits on the {Staircase} of the {Mint} as a giant *yuan coin* rolls down towards him, bump, bump, bump. It splits into ten, then a hundred smaller **yuan**, jingling over every step. The yogi stacks them into a wobbly tower and balances on top, paying one **yuan** a minute for the view.

On the {Rooftop} above the {Boxing Ring}, the {Yogi} meets a *hero* in a bowler hat holding a teacup. Instead of punching, the hero apologises, queues politely and offers the villain a biscuit. The crowd roars: how terribly **British**! Soon even the pigeons are saying sorry and sipping tea, very **British** indeed.

The {Sheriff} lifts the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} and finds a *scholar* in spectacles, buried in books about honey. The **scholar** has measured every hexagon and written ten volumes on buzzing. The bees, deeply impressed, crown him with a wax mortarboard, and now the sheriff must bow and call him the Honourable **Scholar**.

The {Jockey} pops out of a {Trapdoor} in the {Jungle} just as a monkey kicks a coconut over a *goal line*. A *small speech bubble* snaps a photo: flash! Here is the **proof**, it squeaks, it was a goal! The gorilla goalkeeper demands more **proof**, so the bubble replays it in slow motion on a banana leaf.

The {Juggler} pops up through a {Trapdoor} in the {Inn}'s kitchen, where a lumberjack swings an *axe* to chop a long *road* shorter. Chop! Now the next town is **near**. Chop! Now it is right outside the door. Chop! Now it is so **near** that its church bell is ringing in the dining room.

The {Sheriff} fires a *lost arrow* from the {Rooftop} of the {Beehive}, and it immediately forgets where it is going. It wanders over hills, asks a cow for directions, and **loses** its feathers on the way. By sunset the sheriff has **lost** his arrow, his hat, and finally his temper.

In the {Basement} under the {Swan Pond}, the {Jockey} rides a *cart* bolted to a giant *spindle*. It starts to **turn**, slowly, then faster and faster, until the jockey is a blur and the swans upstairs spin on the water like ballerinas. Every time he tries to stop, the spindle **turns** the other way.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Pool}, the {Firefighter} is getting married, and her *husband* climbs the ladder in a tuxedo and flippers. Her new **husband** slides down the fire pole to the reception and lands in the pool with the cake. She dives in after him, laughing, because a **husband** who brings cake is worth rescuing.

The {Lifeguard} is refereeing in the {Boxing Ring} when a *herald* bursts up through the {Trapdoor}, unrolls a scroll and blasts a trumpet in her ear. By royal **order**, he reads, all boxers must wear tutus! The lifeguard blows her whistle and gives an **order** of her own: everyone into the pool, tutus and all.

In the {Casino}'s {Basement}, the {Jockey} bets on a *sparrow* that flicks *icicles* at a dartboard with its beak. Bullseye, bullseye, bullseye: perfectly **accurate** every time. The croupier tries to distract it with breadcrumbs, but the sparrow just spears each crumb in mid-air, still dead **accurate**, and the jockey wins the whole casino.

The {Baker} opens a {Trapdoor} in the {Pool}'s floor and pulls out an endless roll of *linen*. He keeps pulling: metres of **cloth**, then kilometres, until the pool is draped like a giant tent. Swimmers splash about under a ceiling of **cloth**, and he uses one corner to wrap a loaf the size of a car.

In the {Basement} of the {Beehive}, the {Sheriff} sits in the front row as a *woman* steps onto a tiny *stage* and claps her hands. Let the show **begin**! Bees swirl, lights flash, the curtain rises. Then she claps again and it all **begins** again from the start, and the sheriff falls asleep during the third beginning.

In the {Basement} of the {Funfair}, the {Zookeeper} winds a *jack-in-the-box* until it bursts open and out bounces a big red cartoon *heart*. **How**? he gasps. **How** does a heart fit in a toy box? The heart just shrugs, hops on the carousel and asks him how he fits in a basement.

The {Ninja} sits on the {Front Step} of a {Hut} beside a *nun* whose *mouth* tacks a **question particle** onto every sentence. Nice weather, ne? A biscuit, ne? Each ne floats up like a bubble with a question mark on it. The ninja is so busy answering every **question** that he forgets he came to sneak, and stays for tea.

The {Tsar} tiptoes down the {Staircase} of the {Casino} carrying a *piggy bank* the size of a pony. Instead of gambling, he **deposits** every chip, coin and jewel he finds into its slot, clink, clink. The pig grows fatter and fatter until it squeals, and the tsar makes one final **deposit**: his crown.

The {Wizard} pops out of a {Trapdoor} on an island in the {Lake} and taps a *sapling* with his wand. Are you a mighty oak yet? **Not yet**, squeaks the sapling. He waits a minute. Now? **Not yet**. He waits a hundred years, with a beard down to his toes, and the sapling still whispers, not yet.

In the {Basement} of the {Mint}, the {Yogi} rolls a *yuan coin* onto a *road* painted on the floor. It rolls and rolls, out of the door, across the country, over the sea. The yogi meditates while it travels **far**, **far** away, and three years later gets a postcard from it, from somewhere very far indeed.

The {Juggler} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Cat Café} and finds a giant *mouth* tangled in a *twisted vine*, **calling** every cat in town. Here, kitty kitty! it booms. Hundreds of cats pour in through the windows. Then the mouth **calls** the juggler's name too, and he comes running on all fours, like a cat.

The {Tailor} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Island} lighthouse and sews a *stage* out of curtains and sailcloth. It stiffens into a solid **platform** jutting out over the sea. Whales gather to watch as he struts up and down the **platform**, showing off a new swimsuit for seagulls.

The {Dentist} plays tennis on the {Rooftop} of the {Mansion} with one huge *racket* and one **single** ball. No partner, no net, no opponent, only him whacking the ball off the chimney. The butler brings out a second racket, but the dentist refuses: this is a **singles** match, a **single** dentist against a chimney.

In the {Basement} under the {Boxing Ring}, the {Yogi} dips a brush's *bristles* in paint and flicks a whole *landscape* onto the wall: hills, rivers, a sunset. The **image** comes alive, and a painted cow wanders out to drink from the water bucket. The boxers upstairs keep sneaking down to stare at the moving **image**.

The {Juggler} drops through a {Trapdoor} into the {Museum} clutching a *toolbox* that won't stay shut. It snaps open and fires out every **tool** at once: hammers, spanners, a saw, a drill. He juggles them all above a priceless vase, and the guards hold their breath until the last **tool** lands safely in his pocket.

The {Lifeguard} stands on the {Staircase} of the {Warehouse}, swinging a *gauze net* at everything that floats by. She **collects** loose buttons, lost socks, runaway kites and a confused bat. By the top step the net bulges, and she **collects** one last thing: the warehouse manager, who was only passing.

The {Zookeeper} opens the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} and finds a *child* sitting under a tiny *roof*, painting Chinese **characters** on the bees with a brush. Every bee buzzes off wearing a different word. Then the whole hive flies in formation and spells one enormous **character** across the sky: the word for honey.

The {Ghost} floats up through a {Trapdoor} on a lonely {Island} and meets a new *friend*: a coconut with a painted smile. He falls in **love** at once. He writes it poems, carves hearts in the sand and twirls it round in the moonlight. The coconut says nothing at all, but the ghost is sure it is **love**.

On the {Rooftop} of a hut on the {Beach}, the {Juggler} is juggling when a giant *punch* in a boxing glove drops out of the sky. Bam! It **strikes** a coconut, a sandcastle, a beach ball. He catches it and juggles it, and it **strikes** again, knocking his own ice cream into orbit.

The {Lifeguard} watches *water drops* begin to trickle down the {Staircase} of the {Youth Hostel}, then gush. A *tumbling baby* in a rubber ring rides the waves, giggling. The water **flows** past bunk beds, through the kitchen and out of the door, and the baby **flows** with it all the way to the sea, waving.

The {Baker} opens a {Trapdoor} on the frozen {Lake}, and his *trudging feet* march him off to a *rice field* on the shore. He **prepares** for winter: harvests every grain, bakes a thousand rice cakes and stacks them in an igloo. The squirrels watch, impressed, and beg him to help them **prepare** too.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Boxing Ring}, the {Baker} drills his *troops*: a line of gingerbread **soldiers** with icing helmets. Left, right, left! They march in perfect step, salute, and charge at a pigeon. The pigeon gobbles the front row, and the last brave **soldier** bites it on the toe.

On the {Staircase} of the {Yen Exchange}, the {Lifeguard} blows her whistle and a *convoy* of tiny trucks drives up the steps. Each truck **links** onto the one in front with a hook, until the chain wraps round the building twice. She ties on a long rope and **links** the last truck to the moon.

The {Dentist} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Cat Café} into a room humming with a giant electric *circuit*. A *small speech bubble* rides along the wires and announces: You are being **transferred**! Zap: the dentist is **transferred** to a cat basket, a cat lands in his dentist's chair, and nobody is happy about it.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Funfair}'s helter-skelter, the {Sheriff} drops a coin down a hole and hears *water drops* echoing from a *deep cave* far below. He jumps in after it. Down he slides, past the dodgems, past the rock, **deeper** and deeper, until he splashes into a lake so **deep** that the fish wear miners' helmets.

The {Sheriff} climbs onto the {Rooftop} of the {Hangar} and finds a *skylight* propped open, with a **merchant** selling goods through it to the pilots below. Parachutes, peanuts, slightly used clouds! he cries. The sheriff tries to arrest him for blocking the light, but the **merchant** sells him a badge, a moustache and the skylight itself.

The {Sailor} rises through a {Trapdoor} in the {Swan Pond} on a raft of *bamboo*, clacking a giant *abacus*. He **calculates** everything: how many swans, how many feathers, how many breadcrumbs per beak. The swans line up for their share, and one argues so hard that he has to **calculate** it all again, using its long neck as the abacus.

The {Jockey} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} as an inspector taps a golden *shell* with a *pair of axes*. Ting! Top **quality**. Next shell: clunk, poor **quality**, into the bin. The bees queue nervously with their honey shells, and the queen's shell rings so perfectly that the axes bow to her.

On the {Staircase} beside the {Swan Pond}, the {Tailor} builds a little *fence* around a single *green shoot*. Soon every swan, duck and frog crowds inside the fence to admire it, a whole **group** jostling and honking. The tailor measures them all and sews matching **group** uniforms, each with a hole for the shoot.

The {Juggler} sits on a driftwood {Staircase} on the {Beach} and whistles, and every *sparrow* for miles flies in to **gather** in one *tree*. Hundreds, then thousands, until the tree bends like a fishing rod. More birds **gather** on his head, his arms, his juggling clubs, until he has to juggle the sparrows instead.

In the {Basement} of a shack on the {Island}, the {Baker} finds a *banknote* poking out of the floorboards. He pulls it, and out comes another, and another: a **hundred** banknotes, tied in a line like a magician's hankies. He bakes them into a **hundred** loaves, and the coconuts queue up to buy one.

The {Shepherd} is stuck on the {Rooftop} of the {Museum}, *waiting in rain* with forty soggy sheep. They **need** an umbrella. They **need** a towel. They need hot cocoa, a hairdryer and a ladder. At last a marble goddess leans out of her niche and hands them exactly what they **need**: one very large bath towel.

The {Juggler} pops out of a {Trapdoor} in the {Piazza} to buy an ice cream, but the vendor refuses to talk to him. A *go-between* runs back and forth, and a *standing person* shouts the new **price** each time: one coin, two coins, a hat, a goat. By the time they agree, the **price** is the juggler's entire act.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Water Park}, the {Hunter} chases a *shape-shifter* through a patch of *grass*. It turns into a frog, then a snail, then, just as he pounces, a huge pink **flower**. He cannot shoot a **flower**, so he tucks it in his hat, and it winks at him all the way down the slide.

In the {Basement} of the {Hangar}, the {Dentist} finds his *big brother* wearing a *lampshade* on his head and leading a political **party**. Vote for free dental floss! he shouts, and the mice cheer. By midnight the whole basement has joined the **party**, and the dentist is elected Minister of Teeth.

The {Hunter} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Water Park}'s tallest slide, and *fireworks* burst out of every step he touches. Gold, crimson, emerald: the whole park lights up in a **splendid** display. He whooshes down in a shower of sparks, and the crowd agrees it is the most **splendid** exit anyone has ever made.

On a mossy {Staircase} in the {Jungle}, the {Chef} piles up *soil* into walls and towers and plants a golden *trophy* on top. Monkeys move in, then parrots, then tapirs with briefcases, until it is a bustling **city** with traffic lights. The trophy goes to the best **city** in the jungle, which is also the only one.

The {Sheriff} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Beehive} and trips over a *stone*. He kicks it, and it kicks back. Suddenly every step turns to **stone**, the honey turns to **stone**, and the bees bounce about as tiny grey pebbles. The sheriff is the only soft thing left, and the stones roll him gently back down.

The {Juggler} races up a {Staircase} cut into the cliff at the {Beach}, towed by a *silk thread* while a *chaser* thunders behind. Every step is a new **level**, like a video game: crabs on the first, seagulls on the second, a sandcastle dragon on the third. At the top **level**, the chaser turns out to be his own shadow.

In a {Basement} under the {Jungle}, the {Jockey} watches a *drill sergeant* march the **whole** jungle up to a *goal line*: every ant, every elephant, every vine. Nobody gets left out! he barks. When a single leaf drifts behind, he marches the **whole** jungle back to the start to begin again.

In the {Basement} of the {Pool}, the {Firefighter} discovers a tiny marble *mansion* where frogs in suits are running the **government**. They pass laws about splashing and put taxes on rubber ducks. When she tries to drain the pool, the entire **government** hops out to hold an emergency meeting on her helmet.

The {Lifeguard} spots a *goblin* sneaking down the {Staircase} to the {Beach} and blows her whistle: **leave**, now! The goblin packs one sandcastle, two towels and a crab into a tiny suitcase. It waves goodbye, climbs onto a seagull and **leaves**, then comes back three times to wave again.

The {King} pops up through a {Trapdoor} in the {Swamp} to find his *big brother* frozen in a block of *icicles*, croaking for help. What is the **situation**? asks the king. The **situation**, his brother explains, is that the swamp froze, the frogs went skating, and he is stuck as a rather royal ice lolly.

The {Yogi} rises from a {Trapdoor} in the {Spa} wearing a *silver medal* the size of a frying pan. He won it in a race across all of **Asia**, stretching from one end to the other in a single yoga pose. Steam paints a giant map of **Asia** above the hot tub, and he lies down on it for a nap.

In the {Basement} of the {Boxing Ring}, the {Cheerleader} **invites** the whole town to a party, writing each card on soft green *moss* and handing it to a *small speech bubble*. The bubbles float off and squeak at every door, You are **invited**! By nine the basement is packed with boxers, grannies and one bewildered moose.

The {Juggler} emerges from a {Trapdoor} on the {Beach} and balances a *branch* on his nose while a *helping hand* tosses him coconuts. He catches them on the twigs, one, two, ten, without dropping any. Pure **skill**! cry the crabs. Then the hand throws in a jellyfish, and his **skill** gets very wobbly indeed.

The {Juggler} pops up through a {Trapdoor} on the {Beach}, wedged **between** a *hillside* and a stone *altar*. He cannot move left or right, so he juggles straight up. Gulls dart **between** his juggling pins, crabs scuttle between his toes, and he stays squashed between the two until the tide floats him free.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Ice Rink}, the {Yogi} ties a *promise knot* in his beard to remember an **appointment**. Then he forgets what the knot is for. He ties another, and another, until his beard is a tangle of knots and he has missed every **appointment** in town, including the one with his barber.

The {Sheriff} opens the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} and finds the bees gathered round an *altar*, where the queen is **showing** off her new crown under a spotlight. Then every bee **shows** something: a dance, a drawing, a jar of jam. Put on the spot, the sheriff **shows** them his badge, and they faint with admiration.

The {Firefighter} slides through a {Trapdoor} at the bottom of the {Pool} and pops out in Antarctica. She grabs a ticket for the *return trip* and **returns** at once, dripping and snowy. But the trapdoor flings her off again, so she spends all day **returning**, with a penguin who is starting to enjoy the commute.

The {Baker} drops through a {Trapdoor} into the {Boxing Ring} and lands on a *sickbed* balanced on a wobbly *tripod*. He has caught a strange **illness**: every sneeze shoots out a bread roll. The boxers duck and dodge the rolls, and the referee declares the **illness** the winner by knockout.

On the {Rooftop} of a lifeguard tower on the {Beach}, the {Shepherd} lies down with his sheep for a **rest**. Every slow *breath* he takes puffs out a tiny cloud, and the sheep float up onto them, snoring. Soon the whole flock is **resting** on clouds above the sea, and nobody wants to come down.

The {Juggler} prises open the {Rooftop} of the {Youth Hostel} with a *crowbar* and finds a *cave* hidden in the attic, full of muddy footprints. He **investigates** with a magnifying glass, sniffing, measuring, tasting. The trail leads to a backpacker eating everyone's yogurts, and the juggler **investigates** him so closely that he confesses.

The {Shepherd} pops up through the {Trapdoor} of the {Yen Exchange}, unrolling a *silk thread* behind him. *Twin blades* snip it into neat pieces, and he lays them across the trading floor in one dead-straight **line**. Every banker must now stand on the **line**, and the sheep patrol to check that nobody wobbles.

The {Sailor} opens the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} and spots a *standing person* holding a *tool*. It **seems** to be a spoon. Then it **seems** to be a trumpet, then a toothbrush, then a small grumpy hedgehog. Nothing is what it seems, and the bees insist the person only **seems** to be a person: really, it is a very large bee.

On the {Rooftop} of the bandstand by the {Swan Pond}, the {Gardener} meets an *official* in a tall hat, stamping papers. Every swan needs a permit to paddle, the **official** announces, stamping each beak. Soon the gardener needs a permit to garden, a permit to sneeze, and a permit to complain to the **official**.

In the {Basement} of the {Warehouse}, the {Hunter} lights a tiny *campfire* to toast one marshmallow. The **fire** gobbles the marshmallow, then the bag, then a crate of fireworks. Whoosh! Rockets zoom round the basement, and the hunter roasts sausages over the **fire** while sprinting in circles.

The {Dentist} rises through a {Trapdoor} in the {Swan Pond} and swings an *axe* at a stuck rowing boat. Crack! The oar **breaks**. Crack! The jetty **breaks**. He swings once more and **breaks** the boat, a bread roll and the swans' concentration, and they all sulk in pieces.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Boxing Ring}, the {Juggler} boils *rice* and *moss* in a giant kettle until only one glowing drop remains: pure **essence**. He takes a single sniff and juggles faster than ever. The boxers below catch the smell and start dancing ballet, because the **essence** of everything, it turns out, is ballet.

In the {Basement} of the {Mansion}, the {Magician} taps a teacup and *water drops* start pouring out of it, endlessly. The cup is **full**, the sink is full, the basement is **full**, and the butler is swimming laps. The magician pulls a rabbit out of the water, and even the rabbit is **full** of water drops.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Beehive}, the {Jockey} wedges a forked *branch* under the sagging ceiling just in time. The branch **supports** the roof, the queen's throne and a very heavy jar of honey. Then all the bees pile on top to cheer, and the branch groans, but keeps **supporting** them all.

The {Sheriff} lifts the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} and finds a *watcher* kneeling before a *small altar* with a telescope on it. The watcher **looks at** the sheriff. The sheriff **looks at** the watcher. Then both slowly turn to **look at** the telescope, which, it turns out, has been looking at them all along.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Cat Café}, the {Shepherd} paints a *portrait* of a stormy sea, and real *water drops* splash out of the canvas, flooding the roof. He paints a sun, and the flood **subsides**. He paints a sleepy cat, and the waves **subside** to a purr, then to a puddle that the cats lick dry.

The {Yogi} opens a {Trapdoor} in the {Ice Rink}, and a *runner* skates out waving a *ceremonial axe*. **The more** she twirls it, the faster she skates; **the more** she skates, the louder the crowd cheers; and the louder they cheer, the more she twirls. Soon she is a whirlwind, and the yogi is very dizzy.

The {Cheerleader} pops out of a {Trapdoor} on the {Beach} with a strange **device** strapped to a *dog*: four horns and a crank. When the dog wags, the horns sing like a *chorus*, in perfect harmony. Sunbathers dance along, and the cheerleader patents the **device** as the world's first barking orchestra.

The {Robot} clanks down a {Staircase} into the {Lagoon} carrying an empty *container*. It scoops in fish, coral, a shipwreck, a whale and finally the whole lagoon. Somehow the container **contains** it all and still has room. The robot peeks inside to see what else it can **contain**, and falls in.

The {Jockey} climbs through the {Trapdoor} at the top of the {Tower} and blows on a pile of *embers* until they glow. He feeds them into a giant *spotlight*, and it **shines** over the whole city: bats squint, owls put on sunglasses. He points it at the moon, which starts **shining** twice as bright to say thank you.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Museum}, the {Shepherd} finds a *page* of rules tied to a brush full of stiff *bristles*. Rule one: every sheep **must** be brushed. Rule two: every sheep **must** be brushed again. So he brushes all forty sheep into fluffy clouds, because rules are rules and sheep **must** sparkle.

In the {Basement} of the {Youth Hostel}, the {Juggler} prises open a crate with a *crowbar*, and out pop exactly **nine** cats, each wearing a little backpack. Each cat has **nine** lives, so he does the sum while juggling them all: eighty-one lives, purring at once, and not one of them has paid for a bed.

On the {Rooftop} of a treehouse in the {Jungle}, the {Zookeeper} pours *soil* into a bamboo *steamer* and pops the lid on. Puff! The soil doubles. Puff! It doubles again. Each burst of steam **increases** the pile until it buries the treehouse and the monkeys open a ski resort, and still it **increases**.

The {Yogi} sits on the {Staircase} of the {Mansion} grinding a *stone* with a heavy *door bar*, doing **research** into what is inside it. Dust, more dust, a fossil, a tiny surprised snail. He writes it all up in a notebook, and the butler, inspired, starts doing **research** into the inside of the teapot.

In the {Basement} of the {Yeti Cave}, the {Shepherd} finds a yeti hunched over a *writing desk*, **writing** a long letter with an icicle. The ink freezes, so every word **written** pops off the page like an ice cube. The shepherd scoops them into a bucket and drops them in his tea, one sentence at a time.

On the {Rooftop} of a temple in the {Jungle}, the {Chef} hangs a *wind chime* made of *grain stalks*, and every time it tinkles it **names** a passing animal. Bob! it chimes at a tapir. Gertrude! at a tiger. Soon every creature in the jungle has a **name**, and the chef has to write them all on a menu.

In a {Basement} dug under the {Beach}, the {Cheerleader} finds a *person* standing beside a *stop sign*, running a tiny **enterprise**: selling stop signs to crabs. Business is booming. Soon the **enterprise** has offices, a logo and a board of crab directors, and every crab on the beach stops politely before crossing.
